entries.title: Complex-description boundary in end-to-end 3D world construction
entries.frozen_irreducible_object: A measurable failure-regime boundary in end-to-end multimodal world construction: after RL raises overall executable 3D construction performance, long underspecified Complex Description and Scene Restatement queries remain below 50% Pass@1. The scientific object is not query difficulty in general, but the transition between queries that can be solved by the trained intent-layout-tool-render-reflect loop and those that fail despite broad 3D-reasoning gains.
entries.frozen_endpoint_headroom_requirement: To remain paperable beyond a benchmark observation, the candidate needs a prospective pre-outcome feature or controlled intervention that predicts the below-50% basin and separates executable cross-stage binding from long-context, generic underspecification, and spatial-grounding baselines.
entries.frozen_exact_prediction: After matching prompt length, number of constraints, referential ambiguity, asset count, rubric difficulty, and spatial-quantity demand, Complex Description/Scene Restatement queries will still show lower Pass@1 and a higher concentration of cross-stage intent-to-layout/render binding failures than other VWE-Bench query types; clarifying text alone will not close the gap unless it also resolves executable binding.
entries.frozen_same_information_baseline: A matched long-context plus spatial-grounding baseline that uses query length, constraint count, ambiguity, asset count, distance/angle/object-count demands, and stage-specific grounding/editing errors to predict Pass@1.
entries.frozen_falsifier_expression: Using released VWE-Bench/VibeWorlding-Gym units, construct a matched comparison: sample Complex Description/Scene Restatement failures and easier-query controls matched on length, constraint count, asset count, rubric difficulty, and spatial-quantity demand; annotate stage-specific errors; optionally generate clarified-query versions. The falsifier is passed if query type no longer predicts Pass@1 or stage-specific binding failure after these controls.

prior_support.required_unit: VWE-Bench per-case query metadata sufficient for matching plus first-party per-case Pass@1/model outcome and preferably stage-specific failure labels.
prior_support.asset_audit: Official VibeWorlding-Gym code was cloned at ddb6ff54d34a2483859960743319f5d5e5b33e96. README declares 6,828 VWE-Bench queries and 254 evaluation cases, but the GitHub checkout contains data placeholders; this run did not materialize the Hugging Face query corpus or first-party per-case model outcome table. Code release alone cannot instantiate the frozen matched boundary falsifier.
prior_support.reopen_only_if: First-party VWE-Bench query units and per-case model/evaluator outcomes can be materialized with content hashes so matching and stage-error analysis are independent of the candidate claim.

entries.title: Stateful-feedback validity horizon for self-evolving skill controllers
entries.frozen_irreducible_object: A feedback-validity horizon object for self-evolving agents: given the same initial controller/update schedule and observable early-feedback state, predict whether later persistent-state changes will make the schedule invalid because newly exposed multi-turn defects lie outside the initial error basis. The object must separate feedback-source exhaustion from ordinary nonstationarity, stale supervision, and governance/action-surface changes.
entries.frozen_endpoint_headroom_requirement: The residual must appear on prospective later-round defects before observing endpoint TSR, not by post hoc selection of trajectories where multi-turn feedback wins. It must survive matched feedback quantity, recency, task difficulty, governance action, and harness-state statistics.
entries.frozen_exact_prediction: Under matched model, task distribution, initial feedback, update budget, and harness-state statistics, an update schedule selected from initial single-turn feedback will fail or stagnate when later multi-turn interactions reveal defects outside the initial feedback basis; a stateful feedback-refresh controller will improve on those same units. A generic stale-supervision/nonstationarity baseline given the same feedback recency and occupancy statistics will not predict the basis-mismatch split.
entries.frozen_same_information_baseline: A stale-supervision/nonstationary online-learning baseline that receives the same early and later feedback samples, recency, sample size, occupancy/domain-shift statistics, and update budget, and predicts performance solely from distribution shift and fresh-information availability.
entries.frozen_falsifier_expression: Using the released or reproducible SkillEvo substrate, create matched units with the same initial single-turn feedback and early TSR trajectory. In one arm, keep later defects within the initially revealed gap classes; in the other, introduce later multi-turn defects outside that class while matching task difficulty, model, revision budget, governance, and feedback quantity. Compare an initial-feedback-selected schedule against a stateful feedback-refresh schedule and a generic stale-supervision/nonstationarity baseline. If the generic baseline predicts the split equally well, reject the new problem formulation.

prior_support.required_unit: SkillEvo round-level units exposing the same initial single-turn feedback basis, later multi-turn defect classes, revision schedule, TSR/defect outcomes, and a reproducible controller or first-party code/data sufficient to construct matched within-basis versus outside-basis units.
prior_support.asset_audit: As of 2026-08-24, source review found the SkillEvo paper and aggregate results over 9 production Skills and 98 skill-reference files but no verified maintained first-party repository or released unit-level dataset sufficient for the frozen matched horizon falsifier. Aggregate TSR curves cannot establish feedback-basis mismatch.
prior_support.reopen_only_if: A first-party SkillEvo repository/dataset or provenance-equivalent unit-level release exposes feedback/revision trajectories needed for matched inside-basis versus outside-basis analysis.
